uiSettings.intro: Tool settings that don't affect maps. Changes are applied immediately.
uiSettings.heading: Generator settings:
uiSettings.interfaceSizeTip: Set user interface size. Browser zoom also affects interface size (Ctrl + or Ctrl - to change).
uiSettings.themeColorTip: Set theme hue for dialogs and tool windows.
uiSettings.restoreThemeColor: Restore default theme color: pale magenta.
uiSettings.radarChartColorTip: Set the color used for Character Details radar charts.
uiSettings.restoreRadarChartColor: Restore default radar chart color: blue.
uiSettings.transparencyTip: Set dialog and tool windows transparency.
uiSettings.autosaveTip: Set autosave interval in minutes. Set 0 to disable autosave. The map is saved in browser storage.
uiSettings.onloadTip: Set what Generator should do on load.
uiSettings.assistantTip: Toggle Azgaar Assistant (help bubble in the lower-right corner).
uiSettings.zoomLevelTip: Show the current map zoom level in the lower-left corner.
uiSettings.speakerVoiceTip: Select a text-to-speech voice. Click the test button to preview it.
uiSettings.emblemShapeTip: Select emblem shape. It can be changed individually in the Emblem editor.
uiSettings.zoomExtentTip: Set minimum and maximum possible zoom level.
uiSettings.minZoom: Minimum possible zoom level (must be greater than 0).
uiSettings.maxZoom: Maximum possible zoom level (must be greater than 1).
uiSettings.allowDragBeyondCanvas: Allow dragging the map beyond canvas borders.
uiSettings.populationRenderingTip: Select the population layer visualization style.
uiSettings.heightmapRenderingTip: Select how Heightmap is drawn in SVG mode. WebGL Hybrid always uses its optimized terrain renderer.
uiSettings.combatDeathsRenderingTip: Select how recent combat deaths are drawn (the time window matches Population Overview Deaths).
uiSettings.renderingTip: Select rendering model. Try optimized mode if you face performance issues.
uiSettings.languageTip: Choose the display language. English remains the fallback language.
uiSettings.configureWorldTip: Open World Configurator to set the map position on the globe and world climate.
uiSettings.resetDefaultsTip: Restore default options and reload the page.

about.costOfLivingIntro: This world uses one shared coinage: gold pieces 🟡, silver pieces ⚪, and copper pieces 🟤. Prices, treasury balances, and personal wealth are stored as silver-piece values and displayed as coinage. Grain trades at roughly one silver piece per wain at market (farmgate prices run about 20% lower), anchoring the currency's baseline value. The figures below are storytelling guidelines, not exact simulated totals; actual prices vary with local market conditions.
about.costOfLivingPeasant: One peasant (rural resident), bare subsistence for a year: roughly 4–5 copper pieces at the default exchange rates — just enough grain to survive, based on the world's per-capita food need.
about.costOfLivingUrban: One town or city resident, for a year: roughly 5–10 copper pieces at the default exchange rates — the same baseline food need, plus higher retail prices and incidental goods city life requires.
about.costOfLivingFamily: One family of four or five, for a year: roughly 2–4 silver pieces — the sum of each member's living cost.
about.costOfLivingHouse: A modest house or homestead: roughly 10–30 silver pieces — several years of a laborer's savings. Buying property isn't a simulated transaction yet, so treat this as a storytelling rule of thumb rather than an in-game price.
